title: Compressed Air Tank Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.169)
subtitle: Use for each air receiver when it is installed and at every routine site inspection.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A for each air receiver, and note the receiver's location or ID.
For any Defect, record what you found, report it to the person responsible for the compressed air system and have it corrected.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Construction code
items: A receiver installed after the effective date of the regulations is constructed to ASME BPVC Section VIII, 1968 edition
Each safety valve is constructed to ASME BPVC Section VIII, 1968 edition
Each safety valve is installed and maintained to ASME BPVC Section VIII, 1968 edition

sections.title: Location, access and drainage
items: The drain valve, handholes and manholes can all be reached easily, with nothing stored or built in front of them
The receiver is not buried underground and is not in an inaccessible place
A drain pipe and valve are fitted at the lowest point of the receiver
Opening the drain valve empties the receiver completely, and no excessive oil or water collects between drainings
Any automatic trap is fitted in addition to a drain valve, which is still present

sections.title: Pressure gage and safety valves
items: An indicating pressure gage is fitted and readily visible, not hidden or obscured
At least one spring-loaded safety valve is fitted to the receiver
Combined safety valve capacity keeps receiver pressure within 10 percent above its MAWP
No valve of any type sits between the receiver and any of its safety valves

sections.title: Protection and testing of safety appliances
items: No safety valve is blocked, tied or plugged, or set up so it could readily be made inoperative
Indicating and controlling devices are installed so they cannot readily be disabled
Exposure to the elements cannot readily put any safety valve, gage or control out of action
Safety valves are tested frequently and at regular intervals, and the latest test found them in good operating condition

references: 29 CFR 1910.169: Air receivers (Part 1910 Subpart M, Compressed Gas and Compressed Air Equipment)
